test_title: SSC Steno 2022 Official Paper (Held On: 18 Nov 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.**

She said to me, “I was thinking of going out for dinner but had changed my mind later on.”

options.text: She said me that she was thinking of going out for dinner but changed her mind later on.
She said that she thought of going out for dinner but changed her mind later on.
She told me that I was thinking of going out for dinner but changed my mind later on.
She told me that she had been thinking of going out for dinner but changed her mind later on.

solution:
The correct answer is: "**She told me that she had been thinking of going out for dinner but changed her mind later on.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Indirect speech requires a change in tense and pronouns.
 
• **Reporting Verb**: In this case, the reporting verb is "said." When reporting speech indirectly, it's changed to "told."
 
• **Pronouns**: The pronouns need to be adjusted to fit the new context. "I" becomes "she" (the original speaker), and "me" becomes "me" (the listener).
 
• **Tense Change**: The verb tense changes to reflect that the reported speech is in the past. "Was thinking" becomes "had been thinking," and "had changed" remains the same.
 
• **Reporting Clause**: The original sentence is introduced by "She said to me." In indirect speech, this can be replaced with "She told me that..."

Hence, **option 4** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1** changes the tense correctly, but uses "she said me" instead of "she told me."
 
• **Option 2** changes the tense correctly, but changes the meaning by using "she thought of going out" instead of "she was thinking of going out."
 
• **Option 3** changes the pronouns correctly, but incorrectly states that "I" was thinking of going out.
